WSP Parsons Brinckerhoff and DNV GL (2015). Industrial Decarbonisation and Energy Efficiency Roadmaps to 2050 - Ceramic Sector. Report and Appendices, prepared for the Department of Energy and Climate Change (DECC) and the Department for Business, Innovation and Skills (BIS), London, March 2015.

Source = Ceramic_Report.pdf (main, 90 printed pages) + Ceramic_Appendices.pdf (appendices A-D, 84 printed pages), one source; moved as wsp_2015_uk-roadmap-ceramic.pdf and wsp_2015_uk-roadmap-ceramic-appendices.pdf. Page numbers are PRINTED page numbers (footer "Page N of M"); Appendix C Table 14 (applicability and fuel use, p.62-69) and Table 15 (cost, p.70-73) pages cited per row. Loaded: all 39 options of the Appendix C register (subsector keys All, B heavy clay, R refractories, T technical, W whitewares). Whole technologies (electric kiln and dryer, BAT kilns per subsector, biomass gasification, CC, CHP heat into dryer, oxy-fuel firing) are in the main file with TRL, capex per average site and CO2 saving; the other options are in _measures with gas/biomass/electricity change, TRL, adoption, applicability, capex and site counts. NOT loaded: absolute SEC per tonne (the report gives none; Figures 9-11 are charts), subsector emissions (chart labels, unassigned), pathway deployment and costs. Traps: (1) capex per site is for an AVERAGE site of the subsector; site capacity is not printed (kiln outputs only ~200 t/day heavy clay, ~3 t/day whitewares/refractories, <0.5 t/day technical), so no per-t figures; (2) Table 15 column "% attributable to CO2 reduction" is 50% for new BAT kilns and the electric kiln/dryer: the pathway model counts only half of those costs; (3) Table 14 sign convention (positive = reduction) inferred; the electric kiln row shows electricity use change of -666% and gas 100%; (4) for 2 options (add biomass to clay, avoid firing yellow bricks) no site count is printed; (5) Table 14 column "Source" keys: 1A Cerame-Unie, 1B Carbon Trust, 1C IPPC Bureau, 2 workshop/sector team; (6) price year: the report states costs are in present-day (2015) value; heating-value basis never stated. CC capex is capture equipment on a host kiln (INCLUDES CAPTURE).
